diagnostics.detail: Reader-state JSON was exported only after shared verifier acceptance.
diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A person stated that due to the country's conditions, important life decisions such as having children and buying a house have been postponed. Long-term plans have been canceled, and only daily routines are followed. He believes that the country's situation has made controlling life difficult.

The US military destroyed two small Iranian boats after the IRGC attempted to seize a US Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz. Most of the boat occupants were killed, and search and rescue operations are ongoing. The drone remains under US control.

Golareh Abbasi, a political activist and former political prisoner, announced that her account on Snapp was blocked. Snapp stated the reason for blocking was lack of necessary qualifications for cooperation. Abbasi attributed this action to Snapp's fear.

Ali Falih Al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, met with Friedrich Merz, the Chancellor of Germany, in Berlin on Tuesday, 24 Shahrivar, during his European trip. Al-Zaydi was welcomed at the Chancellor's office. This report was provided by Ahmad Samadi from Iran International.

A person in Iran stated that due to unfavorable economic and political conditions, many important life decisions such as continuing education, changing cars, marriage, and having children have been postponed. He complained about the lack of medical equipment and severe inflation, saying his life is almost halted. Additionally, the news of his wife's pregnancy caused him concern.

Saudi Arabia and Israel are in contact through CENTCOM, and Riyadh has requested intelligence assistance from Israel to counter Houthi attacks. Mohammed bin Salman has asked regional countries for help against the Houthis. The request for help from Israel was made indirectly through the United States.

Tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic continue. The Saudi Crown Prince arrived in Cairo to meet with the President of Egypt. Iran International reporters discussed reactions to the Houthis' threats and missile attacks.

Iran International has increased the display of names and images of more victims of the December protests with a new design. Families and relatives can submit information about the missing victims. More details are provided in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.

The mother of Ramin Hossein Panahi supported the call for a general strike in Kurdistan. This occurred on the eve of the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's government killing. Additionally, the Association of Families of Ukrainian Plane Victims issued a statement supporting the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising.

Today, on 24 Shahrivar, applicants of the National Housing in Kashan held a protest in front of the county governor's office. They demand attention to their requests. They claim that despite paying the required amounts, the housing units have not been delivered to them.

A building under construction on Haft Tir Boulevard in Mashhad caught fire. The spokesperson for Mashhad Fire Department said 14 fire trucks from several stations are at the scene. Firefighting operations are ongoing.

Four Iranian football players, including Alireza Jahanbakhsh, Mehdi Qaedi, Ali Gholizadeh, and Majid Hosseini, have become subject to military service after their previous exemptions expired. They must take necessary actions to resolve their military service status. If they return to Iranian football, they may join military teams.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said in Congress that they have seen positive remarks from the UAE about cutting off Iran's financial resources. He also reported good private talks with China about Iran's financial connections and added that these talks will continue with China's vice premier. Trump and Xi Jinping will also discuss Tehran later this month.

Ehsan Khandozi was appointed as the new head of the economic group of the Supreme Leader's office. His introduction ceremony was held on Tuesday morning, September 13. Khandozi was previously a representative of Tehran in the 11th parliament and served as the Minister of Economy in Ebrahim Raisi's government.

On Monday, 23 Shahrivar, the Intelligence Corps agents searched Raha Jalilian's home and confiscated some digital devices belonging to her family. Raha Jalilian was simultaneously summoned to the Intelligence Corps. The agents were unable to arrest her due to her absence.

The public running event in Kerman province was canceled following protests from the seminary about men and women running together. The cancellation was made under pressure from government institutions. An interview was conducted with Mehdi Rostampour, a sports journalist.

Mohammadjavad Fardous Khabazi and Amir Mohammad Ostaddoost were shot and killed on January 8, 2026, in Ramsar. Mohammadjavad Fardous Khabazi's mother lit a candle in their memory. This incident took place in Ramsar.

An Italian recreational ship will serve as a floating home for thousands of athletes and officials at the Nagoya Asian Games. This measure is due to the absence of a dedicated athletes' village. It is a different approach to hosting Asia's largest sporting event.

Ahead of the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, Nagoya port will host a luxury cruise ship that will serve as accommodation for athletes. The ship will be used as the floating village for the games from September 14 to October 6. This report was prepared by Somayeh Mehri.

Sirvan Habibi, a citizen from Sanandaj, was arrested on Wednesday, September 8, by intelligence officers in Kamyaran and transferred to an unknown location. About a week later, his family remains unaware of his status and whereabouts. This has increased the concern of his family and close ones.

Iraq's Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi stated that Iraq's oil sales have been severely affected by the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. He also mentioned that the crisis between the Islamic Republic and the United States has impacted the entire world. The German Chancellor said the coalition government will explore ways to help consumers cope with rising fuel prices.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said that the United States never expected to be defeated by the Islamic Republic. He added that during the 40-day war, the US intended to take security action against Tehran from the Kurdistan region of Iraq, but this plot failed. Ghalibaf also emphasized that the US and Israel seek to create discord between Iran and Iraq.

The Houthis once again attacked the strategic pipeline of Saudi Arabia, and the Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reported the formation of a US-led military coalition in support of Riyadh. Meanwhile, Mohammed bin Salman, in a message to the Egyptian president, said he will not surrender to the blackmail of the IRGC and Houthis in the straits.

Gol Gohar Sirjan drew 0-0 against Al Jazira UAE in their first AFC Champions League match. The game was held at Hissar Stadium in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, and Gol Gohar earned the club's first Asian points. Due to a hosting ban, Gol Gohar plays its home matches in Tajikistan.

Moshe Edri, head of Israel's Atomic Energy Commission, claimed that over 9 tons of nuclear material in Iran are outside the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency. This amount is equivalent to the material needed to build more than 10 nuclear bombs. He also referred to the Iranian regime's threat to destroy Israel.

One night before the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death, reports have emerged about the return of the morality police and plainclothes forces. People are reporting on the state of the streets and the city's lockdown. A program is being held to hear people's accounts of the streets in Iran.

The European Parliament reviewed a report on foreign interference and hybrid threats against member countries. Iran, along with Russia, China, Belarus, and North Korea, was named as a threat in the report. The President of the European Parliament called for the release of two imprisoned sisters in Iran.

Britain, the US, and the Netherlands issued a warning about the CHOSEN BRICK spyware used by agents linked to the Islamic Republic to target opponents and journalists. The spyware can steal emails, messages, and access microphones and social media accounts. The FBI stated that the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic uses this spyware to collect information and harm individuals.

Asieh Ramazani, a mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic forces during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Tehran. Her daughter lit a candle in memory of her mother and all victims of the Zhina Mahsa Amini uprising. This event was shared on social media.

The interrogation session of Mohammad Parsa Golchin, a University of Tehran student, was held at Mashhad Prosecutor's Office. He faces charges including conspiracy against internal security and propaganda against the regime. His bail was increased from two billion to fifteen billion tomans, and he was released after posting bail.

The head of Hamadan University of Medical Sciences reported a shortage of 800 nurses in the province. He also confirmed a shortage of assistant nurses and service staff. The recruitment limitation due to clause 'A' of Article 106 of the Seventh Development Plan has exacerbated this shortage.

Arjin Jandi, a 16-year-old child from the village of Kuper in Piranshahr, was arrested by security forces and subjected to torture for forced confession. The intelligence forces entered his home without a judicial warrant and arrested him. His family has had no information about his whereabouts for four days, and their inquiries have been unsuccessful.

Senior military commanders from the US, Israel, and several Arab countries held a secret meeting in Germany last week to discuss war with the Islamic Republic and regional tensions. The meeting was initiated by Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM. The agenda included plans to increase ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and Israeli military operations.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini, holding the blood-stained flag of the Islamic Republic in protest against the killing of the unnamed martyrs. He said the regime's flag is stained with the blood of brave and innocent people. The citizen emphasized that they will not allow escape from this bloodshed.

Flora Samadani and Ahmad Naeimi, a Baháʼí couple residing in Yazd, have been summoned to the Revolutionary Court of Yazd. They are accused of educational or promotional activities contrary to Islamic law. The court session will be held on Tuesday, 31 Shahrivar 1405.

Nima Akbarpour stated that internet instability and outages have led more users to adopt Starlink. He also mentioned that filtering has imposed significant financial costs on people. Using anonymous VPNs has put users' personal information at risk.

Masoud Jafari, deputy coordinator of the Air Force, said Qatar has not provided clear information about the status of three Iranian pilots in Operation Al-Adid. He added that the Islamic Republic considers the pilots alive and captive until their fate is clarified. The Qatari government must be held accountable.

The prosecutor of Bijar announced the blocking of several active social media pages due to the publication of content against public decency and promoting unveiled behavior. Legal cases have been filed against the administrators of these pages. Four individuals have also been released on bail.

A video showing the birthday ceremony of Farid Ramazani at his grave has been released. Farid Ramazani was shot and killed on January 8 in the Aryashahr neighborhood of Tehran. Security forces targeted his right hand finger and fired a third bullet to his forehead.

Al Ain football team defeated Al Nassr Saudi Arabia 4-0 in the first week of the Asian Elite League. Al Ain's goals were scored by Hossein Rahimi (twice), Sofian Rahimi, and Giakoumakis. Al Nassr lost despite having Cristiano Ronaldo in their lineup.

Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli army, described Hamas as defeated and said the group is currently not firing or responding. The Israeli army controls over 64% of the Gaza Strip. However, it has been warned that Hamas is trying to rebuild its military strength and recruit new forces.

The execution of two prisoners was carried out in the prisons of Dastgerd Isfahan and Ilam. These prisoners were sentenced to death for drug-related crimes and murder. Additionally, a prisoner sentenced to death in Anbarabad was spared from execution due to the victim's family's forgiveness.

The death sentence of Ali Rahimi Rigi, a detainee from the December protests, has been confirmed by the appeals court. He is accused of charges including waging war against God and corruption on earth. Ali Rigi accepted responsibility for the charges from the beginning and defended himself personally.

The United States has confirmed the attack on two Iranian boats and their destruction. This news was published in the audio version of Titrawol with Niusha Saremi. More details are provided in this report.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad stated in the program "Cheshmandaz" that poverty alone is not the cause of protests; injustice, economic gaps, lack of future, and lack of motivation also lead to protests. He added that the Iranian government faces financial incapacity, internal conflicts, and loss of legitimacy.

Workers at the Tazareh coal mine in Damghan and Gilrad company in Rasht reported unpaid wages and insurance dues. Additionally, insurance for some construction workers in West Azerbaijan has been cut off. A labor activist criticized the consequences of this issue.

Today, several protests were held including housing applicants in Kashan and retirees in Isfahan. Yesterday, protests occurred among workers in Sirjan, Ahvaz, and job seekers in Shush. These protests were organized to demand attention to their issues.

Yahya Sari, the spokesperson for the Houthis, stated that Saudi warplanes conducted 52 airstrikes in the past 24 hours on the provinces of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Amran. The Houthi Foreign Ministry declared the right to target Saudi forces' gatherings as legitimate. It also stated that navigation in Bab al-Mandab is safe and rejected Saudi claims about the insecurity of this maritime route.

Mohammad Akraminia, the army spokesperson, said that the US has become a nervous actor in its decline and cannot maintain its hegemony. He added that the recent war showed that the US priority is to protect its own and Israel's interests, not the security of regional countries. Therefore, imported security will never guarantee lasting peace.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, spoke about some countries' attempts to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz with warships and air support. He said Iran's resistance did not allow these actions to succeed easily. These statements reflect Iran's stance in the region.
A viewer criticized the high food prices in a video sent to Iran International. He said people do not go to the streets out of fear of death. He described the living conditions as worse than death.

Britain, the US, and the Netherlands have warned about the spyware "Chosen Break" linked to the Islamic Republic, used to target opponents, activists, and journalists. This malware can steal emails and messages and access social networks, microphones, and device screens. Research, military, and technology institutions have also been targeted.

Farzin Karbasi, a political analyst, said that the continued closure of some Iran-Iraq borders is several times more damaging to Iran's economy than to Iraq's, and Baghdad is not willing to face US economic pressure for a few hundred million dollars in trade. He added that the Iraqi government controls the borders to assert its national sovereignty, although it does not have much control over the Islamic Republic's proxy forces.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, announced that the destroyer USS Rafael Peralta is enforcing the US maritime blockade against Iran in the Arabian Sea. According to CENTCOM, US forces have rerouted 103 commercial vessels as of Tuesday to ensure compliance with the blockade.

Iranians in the UK commemorated the fourth anniversary of the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' movement on Tuesday. They remembered Mahsa Amini and the victims of the 1401 protests. The ceremony also honored the martyrs of the national revolution in 1404.

Masoud Pezeshkian requested mechanisms to facilitate and accelerate the renovation of the naval fleet damaged during the Iran war in the Supreme Council of Marine Industries meeting. He also proposed using the capacity of the Organization of Government Property to support the reconstruction of damaged ships. He emphasized that these supports should be managed so that all eligible parties can benefit from them.

A viewer of Iran International criticized the high prices of food items and the small size of potatoes in a video. He asked whether government officials themselves could use such small potatoes. The video highlights the market situation and product quality.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, shared part of a Pentagon report stating that the idea of Iran being defenseless is incorrect. He said hundreds of buildings and military facilities in the US have been damaged or destroyed, and dozens of aircraft have been lost. Araghchi added that more details will be revealed at the appropriate time.

Reuters reported, citing calculations by the US Congressional Budget Office, that Iran's six-month war has so far cost the United States $38 billion, and this figure will increase by about $3 billion per month. According to the report, the costs are calculated through August 1, and the war is expected to increase US inflation by 0.5 percent in the first quarter of 2027.
Liverpool defeated Tottenham 3-1 in the English Football League Cup. Liverpool's goals were scored by McAllister, Akpom, and Szoboszlai. Tottenham scored for the first time this season.

Real Madrid defeated Elche 3-2 in the sixth week of La Liga. The goals for Real Madrid were scored by Matias Dituro (own goal), Kylian Mbappe, and Carlos Aspe. Elche equalized in the second half, but the winning goal was scored by Carlos Aspe.

The Iran Human Rights Campaign reported the death sentence for Hossein Rasouli-Nasab. This sentence concerns detainees from the December 2025 protests. Concerns about the lives of other detainees have increased due to security charges.

The French representative at the Security Council meeting called on the Islamic Republic to stop arming the Houthis and violating the arms embargo. He also urged the Houthis to cease all military actions immediately. The French representative expressed solidarity with the legitimate government of Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

On the anniversary of Mahsa's government killing, suppression forces have returned to the streets. This issue was discussed in a program with Kambiz Hosseini. The audio version of this program has been released.

Hanna Neumann, a Green Party representative in the European Parliament, wrote about the Iranian regime's repression following the death of Zhina Mahsa Amini. She emphasized that the new generation has changed Iran, but the regime remains unchanged. Neumann stated she will work to ensure the European Union continues to support the Women, Life, Freedom movement.

A project called 'Elaj' asks people to report those it calls traitors and send their personal information. This includes collecting names, addresses, jobs, family members' information, and social media accounts. Kambiz Hosseini discusses this topic in a program.

Mozhgan Eftekhari, the mother of Mahsa Zhina Amini, released a message with Mahsa's voice on the eve of the fourth anniversary of her daughter's death. She wrote that Zhina means death is not the end of life. She also emphasized that Mahsa symbolizes the importance of women and girls in society.

Pouria Bakhtiari stated that due to Ebrahim Raisi's misunderstanding of economic concepts, a team created short animations to teach him. Raisi's foundation denied this claim and filed a complaint against Bakhtiari. This issue was discussed in a program hosted by Kambiz Hosseini.

Thomas Massey, a Republican member of the US Congress, has introduced an eight-point resolution to impeach Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War. Massey accuses Hegseth of illegally continuing the war with the Islamic Republic and defying Congress. This report was published by Marzieh Hosseini from Iran International.

The Washington Post reported that the Trump administration is preparing a $2.8 billion weapons package for Israel. This package includes 20,000 MK-84 bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs, and 20,000 I-2000 penetrator warheads.

The Georgian government will stop all flights of Iranian companies to this country starting next Monday, following new US sanctions. The Civil Aviation Organization has not yet announced this. Tour sales to Georgia will only be available until next Sunday.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated that the conflict with the Islamic Republic will enter a completely different phase within one or two months. He said the Islamic Republic will lose more control over the Strait of Hormuz, and ship traffic has returned to over 50% of normal levels. Vance added that the US is not currently conducting offensive operations and that the war will end after the November midterm elections.

The Hengaw human rights organization reported an increased presence of military and security forces in Kurdistan cities ahead of the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death. Military convoys and anti-riot forces have been deployed to Saqez and Sanandaj, and at least 20 Kurdish youths have been arrested in Oshnavieh. Kurdish parties in Iran have called for a general strike, and four Kurdish political prisoners have announced a hunger strike in support.

The Saudi-led coalition announced that its air defense intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone attempting to enter Mecca's airspace. The coalition spokesperson said this was the second attempt by the Houthis to target Mecca. About nine years ago, a ballistic missile was also fired towards Mecca.

CBS News reported that new images it exclusively obtained show for the first time the extent of damage from the Islamic Republic's missile and drone attacks on several US military positions in the Middle East. These images were provided to CBS News by US military personnel, one of whom stated that the extensive damage to US bases has not been disclosed to the American public. The images show damage to Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and Camp Buehring in Kuwait.

CBS News released exclusive images showing extensive damage from Iranian missile and drone attacks on US military bases in the Middle East. The images show a missile strike on an AWACS aircraft at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and destruction of buildings. A US soldier said these damages have not been made known to the American public.

Joe Wilson, a member of the US House of Representatives, reported the interception of a drone belonging to Yemen's Houthis attempting to enter Mecca's airspace. He called the Houthis Iranian proxies and stated that the US stands with Saudi Arabia against this aggression. He also emphasized the coalition of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan to combat the Houthis.

The US representative at the UN condemned the Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, stating that over 90 people were injured. He accused the Islamic Republic of supporting the Houthis and called for an end to their advances. He also urged the Security Council to ensure the implementation of UN resolutions regarding the Houthis.

The human rights organization Hana reported that in the early hours of Wednesday, the Kurdistan Komala Party camp in Zargouzeleh was targeted by a drone attack. The attacking drone was launched from Kermanshah towards the camp. Details of damages and possible casualties are not yet known.

The US State Department, in response to Iran International's question about visas for Islamic Republic officials, said the Trump administration protects the country and American citizens by applying the highest national security and public safety standards in the visa issuance process. It added that it takes seriously its obligations under the United Nations headquarters agreement and has provided guidance to all member states on recommended timelines for visa requests before the 81st General Assembly session. The response did not specify which officials were issued visas or what restrictions might be imposed.

Abdullah Ali Fadhel Al-Saadi, Yemen's representative to the Security Council, said Yemen's armed forces are the first line of defense for global interests in Bab al-Mandab and warned that Houthi attacks should not be seen as a temporary threat. Representatives from Bahrain and the UK condemned the Houthi attacks and called for strict enforcement of arms embargoes. The UK linked the escalation in Yemen to support from the Islamic Republic.

Marco Rubio and Asaad Al-Sheibani held a phone call discussing regional security and increased cooperation between the two countries. The US Secretary of State emphasized the importance of integrating all Syrian minority groups. Rubio also praised Syria's progress in cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency.

The US State Department raised the travel advisory for Saudi Arabia to level 3, advising reconsideration of travel. The warning cites risks of missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic, armed conflict, and terrorism. The border area between Saudi Arabia and Yemen is at level 4, meaning do not travel.

The director of the Nutrition Improvement Office at the Ministry of Health stated that due to the prevalence of short stature in some southern provinces, adding zinc to the supplementation program is under consideration. Children aged 2 to 12 currently receive no supplements. This group requires supplementation interventions due to their rapid growth rate.

Kayhan newspaper criticized some government officials for not recognizing the forces behind the promotion of unveiled behavior and nudity. Kayhan warned that inaction against the cultural invasion of the enemy has negative consequences. The newspaper emphasized that neglect in fulfilling duties related to hijab is unacceptable.

The head of the Food and Drug Administration announced a 103% increase in drug prices and a $900 million reduction in the preferential currency budget. Drug shortages and increased patient payments have made treatment costs heavier for many families. This report was provided by Hadi Zenouzi.

Shayan Samiei said Washington is pursuing four outcomes: stable passage of commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, an end to attacks on US forces and ships, verification of Iran's nuclear program, and reduction of Tehran's missile and drone capabilities.

Senior US military officials have officially confirmed the deployment of active weapons in Earth's orbit for the first time. The Air Force Secretary and Space Force Operations Commander stated these systems are deployed to defend military forces against space-based attacks. More details are provided in an interview with Pasha Majidi.

Jahan Sanat newspaper reported on the impact of rising prices on stationery and school registration costs ahead of school reopening in Iran. Families are concerned about covering these expenses. The report was prepared by Sepid Dana.

CENTCOM confirmed a security meeting of senior commanders from the US, Israel, and eight Arab countries in Germany. The meeting discussed strengthening security cooperation in the Middle East. Commanders from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt, and the Chief of Staff of the Israeli army attended.

The UN Security Council held a meeting to discuss the developments in Yemen and the security crisis in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Several countries' representatives called for an end to the Houthi attacks. The UK representative accused the Islamic Republic of supporting the escalation of tensions in Yemen.

Erfan Ghaneifard said the government fears the name of a martyr, a gravestone, and the silence of the Iranian people. He added that the security arrangements indicate the government is afraid of social mobilization on Mahsa Amini's anniversary. There is also concern about the return of protests to the streets.

The Coordination Council of Iranian Cultural Workers' Associations issued a statement on the fourth anniversary of the Women, Life, Freedom movement, calling it a pivotal moment in Iran's social and political history. The council emphasized that efforts to reinstate the morality police and compulsory hijab are futile. They declared that the movement will not turn back.

Hassan Qashqavi stated that the contradictory behavior of the US makes the change in the Islamic Republic's nuclear doctrine justifiable. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened until the naval blockade is lifted. Additionally, the US requests Iran's cooperation to inspect bombed nuclear sites but has not issued a visa for the head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization.

The Iranian men's national basketball team defeated Bahrain 79-74 and advanced to the semifinals of the Nagoya Asian Games. Mohammad Jamshidi and Mehdi Heydari played key roles in this victory. Iran will face South Korea in the semifinals on Friday, September 17.

Shopkeepers in Saqez closed their shops on September 16. This action coincided with the fourth anniversary of the death of Zhina Mahsa Amini. The presence of military forces in the city has also been reported.

A group of Iranians living in the UK commemorated Zhina Mahsa Amini and other victims of the Iranian protests on September 15 at Trafalgar Square in London. The event was covered through videos sent to Iran International. The gathering was held in support of the protests in Iran.

Israel Katz, Israel's defense minister, stated that the army is ready to complete the destruction of Hamas if ordered. He said Hamas will not be disarmed through an agreement and the army is deployed in various areas of Gaza. Additionally, the US and allied countries have committed to disarming Hamas and destroying tunnels.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin stated that the government has not changed, but society has evolved in progress, goals, and methods. He added that if the government does not change its path, society will gradually change the government. He also noted that on the fourth anniversary of the Women, Life, Freedom movement, society and women have advanced, but the government has not changed any laws.

Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli Army, stated that the army has achieved unprecedented accomplishments in the past three years. He mentioned that the air route to Tehran has been opened and Iran's missile infrastructure has been targeted. Additionally, the capabilities of Hamas and Hezbollah in Gaza and Lebanon have been hit.

On the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death and calls for a strike, armed forces have been deployed in various Iranian cities. Markets and shops in Saqez, Sanandaj, and Kamyaran have been closed, with riot police and armed vehicles present. Reports also indicate checkpoints and arrests of young people in Khash.

Ruhollah Rahimpour stated that the priority of the Americans is to prevent the Islamic Republic from rebuilding its destroyed capacities. He added that economic pressure, financial isolation, and naval blockade could limit the Islamic Republic's ability to rebuild its nuclear and military capacities. Additionally, these pressures affect the continuation of the Islamic Republic's regional activities.

Iran's U23 national football team defeated the UAE 3-1 in their first match at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. Goals were scored by Pouria Shahrabadi and Yousef Mazraeh. Iran will face China and North Korea in the next group stage matches.

The human rights organization HANA reported that on September 16, shopkeepers in Divandareh city, Kurdistan province, went on strike. The strike was held on the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini's death. Videos of the event have been released.

Mohammad Tolaei, former deputy coordinator of the IRGC Intelligence Organization, stated that the collapse of the US and Israel is predestined. He emphasized that this victory will come through the perseverance of the armed forces and the people. Tolaei also mentioned Iran's defensive motivation due to its connection to Ashura.

On the anniversary of Mahsa Amini, cities such as Sanandaj, Saqqez, Kamyaran, and others are experiencing widespread strikes and a heavy presence of military and security forces. Riot police and plainclothes officers have been deployed in the streets, with multiple checkpoints set up in Tehran and other cities. The security atmosphere has intensified in cities like Aligudarz and Khash, with numerous arrests reported.

The fabric sellers' market in Sartpoleh and parts of the Sanandaj market in Kurdistan province went on strike on Wednesday, September 16, to commemorate the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini. The strike took place on September 16. Security measures in Sanandaj have been intensified since September 15.

A number of Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hamburg. The gathering took place on September 15, coinciding with the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Participants chanted the slogan "Long live Iran, long live the Shah."

Elnaz Kompani, an Iranian sprinter, stated that her reason for migrating to the USA is to seek a better future. She wrote on Instagram that she dedicated her youth to Iran and now runs for herself and her future. She emphasized that her heart still beats for Iran and a part of her soul remains in Shiraz.

The human rights organization Hana released a video showing that merchants in Kermanshah went on strike on September 16. This strike was held on the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini's death. The event was recorded by a resident of Kermanshah.

The Israeli army and Shin Bet announced that Nael Abu Ubaid, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, was killed in an airstrike in southern Gaza Strip. Abu Ubaid took command after the death of Mohammad Shabaneh. He was involved in rebuilding Hamas's capabilities and advancing attacks against Israel.
Azad Mohammadi, a citizen from Divandarreh, has been detained for over 50 days. There is still no information about his whereabouts or condition. This situation has caused concerns.

Jose Mourinho admitted that he took a big tactical risk to secure a 3-2 victory against Elche in La Liga. He made offensive substitutions in the final minutes that led his team to win. Mourinho said the risk was necessary because a draw was not enough.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, called the referral of Iran's nuclear file to the Security Council a major mistake by European countries. He warned that if this path continues, Iran might take retaliatory actions. Azizi described the Board of Governors' resolution as political and influenced by the United States.
Videos received show that on September 16, the strike in Sanandaj continues. Police and riot units are deployed in parts of the city. This event coincides with the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini.

Today marks four years since the death of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old woman from Saqez, after being detained by the morality police. Her death sparked widespread protests across Iran, and there has been no effective judicial accountability so far. The UN fact-finding mission stated that her death was caused by physical violence in detention and held the Iranian government responsible.

Shopkeepers and merchants in several Kurdish cities went on strike and closed their shops on the fourth anniversary of the government killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini. Videos showing closed shops in cities such as Sanandaj, Saqqez, Oshnavieh, and others have been released. The presence of military and police forces in some areas has also been reported.

Citizens report a sharp increase in prices of goods and services, difficulties in obtaining medicine, and insufficient wages. Teachers and workers also complain about harsh economic conditions and unpaid dues. The cost of living has risen significantly, causing serious problems for many families.

The parents of Hadis Najafi, a protester killed in the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests, joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. This campaign honors her memory and other victims of the popular uprisings in Iran. A video of this action was shared on social media.

On the fourth anniversary of Mahsa (Zhina) Amini's death, several shopkeepers and merchants in the cities of Baneh, Sanandaj, and Bukan went on strike and refused to carry out their daily activities. The strike took place on the 25th of Shahrivar. This action was taken as a form of protest against the current situation.

Lionel Messi has been called back to the Argentina national team for three friendly matches after his retirement. The matches are against Bolivia, Burkina Faso, and Benin. Messi's invitation may provide a final farewell opportunity with the fans.

Kioumars Heydari, deputy chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, stated that the Islamic Republic's armed forces are undoubtedly victorious in the war. He said Iranian missiles have caused serious damage to heavy US warships. He also added that Iran's strategic plans have led to the enemy's inactivity.

Human rights media reported the establishment of a security and military atmosphere coinciding with a general strike call in Kurdish areas of Iran. Videos show military convoys and riot units moving from Divandareh to Saqqez. This issue was discussed in an interview with Ovin Mostafazadeh, a human rights activist.

Amnesty International released a 1149-page report on the suppression of the "Women, Life, Freedom" protests on the fourth anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini's death. The report accuses the Islamic Republic of committing crimes against humanity. The Amnesty International Secretary-General stated that the evidence leaves no doubt about these crimes.

A retired armed forces member criticized the high cost of medicine in a video to Iran International. He said the government is taking money from the people to send medicine to Hamas and Hezbollah. These medicines are sent to Palestine and Lebanon.

Masoud Farhikhteh, a teachers' union activist, was sentenced to one year of imprisonment and additional punishments while serving his sentence in Karaj Central Prison. The sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj County. A new case was opened against him during his imprisonment.

Joseph Aoun, the President of Lebanon, announced that the country seeks an agreement with Israel. He said the agreement could pave the way for peace and the government wants to keep weapons under its control without causing internal conflict. He also requested help from Europe, the US, and Arab countries to support the Lebanese army to prevent a security vacuum after UNIFIL's withdrawal.

Bartina Koeman, wife of Ronald Koeman, former coach of the Netherlands national team, passed away at the age of 65 after a long battle with cancer. Ronald Koeman announced this sad news in a statement. The football community has also expressed condolences to his family.

Many people have postponed important life decisions such as marriage, medical treatment, and educational migration due to Iran's poor economic conditions. High living costs and inflation have forced people to focus only on daily survival without saving. Additionally, educational migration plans have been halted due to economic difficulties and the lack of required exams.

Videos published on social media show that the sister of Shirin Alizadeh, the mother of Hossein Farhi, and the mother of Atefeh Abed have joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." They honored the memory of the martyrs of the popular uprisings in Iran. This campaign is dedicated to commemorating the victims of public protests.

Mahmoud Rajabi called for the involvement of people, scholars, and the government in combating unveiled behavior. He emphasized the need to create conditions to counter hijab-related disorders and promote the culture of hijab. Rajabi warned that the enemy aims to attack culturally through unveiled behavior and stressed the importance of investing in this area.

Annis Kalamor, Secretary-General of Amnesty International, announced the identification of 87 officials and commanders of the Islamic Republic's security forces. These individuals should be prosecuted for crimes against humanity. This news was presented at Amnesty International's press conference in London.
A silent video received by Iran International shows the closure of shops and a strike by merchants in Oshnavieh city, West Azerbaijan province, on September 16.

Videos received by Iran International show that on September 16, shopkeepers in parts of the city of Mariwan in Kurdistan province were on strike. The strike was observed in some areas of the city. No further details about the cause or extent of the strike have been reported.

Abolfazl Qadyani, a political prisoner, rejected the government's narrative about the role of terrorists in the killing of protesters in December 2025 and held government forces responsible. He questioned why terrorists were absent from government rallies if they were responsible for the killings. Qadyani also named Ali and Mojtaba Khamenei as responsible for the killings.

Anis Kulamar, Secretary-General of Amnesty International, explained in the report on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death that the Iranian people face both repression by the Islamic Republic and the consequences of US and Israeli attacks. He added that the Iranian government has used these conditions to intensify repression and militarize public spaces.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi released a video about the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests and the national Iranian revolution in January 2026, emphasizing that the struggle for Iran's freedom continues. The statement noted that the voices of the fighters are heard from the heart of Iran, and four years after the killing of Mahsa Amini, the commitment to the struggle has been renewed. This fight extends from past uprisings to the Lion and Sun revolution.

The sisters of Babak Sadeghi Mohseni and the family of Behnam Ebrahimi joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." They honored the memory of these immortal individuals. This was seen in videos published on social media.

Mahsa Pirayi spoke at an Amnesty International meeting about her mother, Minoo Majidi's death, emphasizing that justice means accountability. She stated that responsibility should extend to the highest level of the command chain. These remarks were made on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death.

Mahsa Pirayi, daughter of Minou Majidi, spoke at the Amnesty International meeting in London. The event was held on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Mahsa Pirayi is one of the victims of the 1401 protests and the Women, Life, Freedom movement.

Rahim Molaeian, a painter and sculptor residing in Babol, was sentenced to six months of imprisonment by the Revolutionary Court of that city. He was charged with propaganda against the regime. The sentence was issued on September 12.

The Secretary General of Amnesty International in Germany called for judicial investigations into the suppression of protesters in Iran. He emphasized that the perpetrators have not been held accountable and Germany can initiate investigations using the principle of universal jurisdiction. Some victims residing in Germany can provide important evidence.

After the youth match between Sabouri Langarud and Abipoushan Rudsar, protests against the referee's decision led to physical assault. This incident caused the referee's eardrum to rupture. The head of Gilan Football Board announced the case is being pursued and requested action against the guilty coach.

A 10-year-old daughter of the late Ahmad Benvari sang for her father in the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. Ahmad Benvari was killed during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Dezful. The video has been shared on social media.

Austria's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned threats against journalists and emphasized support for media freedom. This stance followed statements by Abolfazl Shekarchi about staff of Iran International, BBC Persian, and Radio Farda. Other international reactions have also come from Germany and Canada regarding these threats.

The head of the judiciary in Rudan announced the suspension and cancellation of fuel cards for 163 vehicles that refueled more than once within 48 hours. This action was based on data from license plate recognition cameras and a judicial order. Smart monitoring of fuel stations continues, and vehicles with repeated irregular refueling will face legal actions.

Various individuals shared their feelings about the first time they went out without mandatory hijab. These feelings included liberation, power, freedom, and gratitude towards those who sacrificed their lives for this cause. Some also experienced comfort and a sense of life changing.

At least eight students at Birjand University have been temporarily banned from studying by the university's disciplinary committee. This ruling was issued by the disciplinary committee. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

Habib Farabbasi, Esteghlal's goalkeeper, will be sidelined for four weeks due to a groin injury. He will miss Esteghlal's match against Tractor in the eighth week of the Premier League. Aria Hosseinifard is the next option for Esteghlal in this position.

The first groups of athletes from various countries entered the Asian Games village in Nagoya, welcomed by Japanese ninjas. Iran's delegation includes over 300 athletes competing in 39 sports. The event took place in rainy weather.

Arash Azarmi from Iran International said China, the UAE, and Iraq are Iran's largest trading partners. The US is trying to limit ways to bypass sanctions by pressuring banks and foreign companies. He mentioned the gradual halt of CoinEx and restrictions on flights from Iran to Georgia.

On Wednesday, 24 Shahrivar, shopkeepers in Mahabad joined a strike on the fourth anniversary of the state killing of Mahsa Amini and closed their shops. This news is based on a video received by Iran International. The strike was held as a symbol of protest.

The Houthi group in Yemen announced that they targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu and an airbase in Khamis Mushait, Saudi Arabia, with dozens of ballistic missiles and drones. These attacks caused extensive fires and significant damage. They emphasized that they will continue their military operations deep inside Saudi territory.
Shopkeepers and merchants in Baneh city, Kurdistan province, closed their shops on Wednesday. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. They stopped working.

Hossein Ghashghaei, his wife Sara Shamsaei, and his brother Abolfazl Ghashghaei were arrested on September 9 by Ministry of Intelligence forces. They have been transferred to Arak, and their place of detention is unknown. Hossein Ghashghaei faces charges including propaganda against the regime and spreading false information.

Following the designation of the IRGC as a terrorist organization in Canada, there are concerns about the rejection of residency applications and deportation of Iranians who served their mandatory military service in the IRGC. About 200 Iranian specialists have written an open letter requesting attention to the situation of these individuals. This report was prepared by Mahsa Mortazavi.

Hassan Rodgar, detained in connection with the December 2025 protests, was transferred to Nowshahr prison to serve his one-and-a-half-year sentence. The sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court of Tonekabon. His transfer took place on the morning of Wednesday, September 15.

A video shows that the strike wave has reached the city of Kamyaran. Several shops and business units in this city in Kurdistan province have been closed. This information was reported by Iran International.
